clue.text: Greek philosopher is alert to change

indicators.note: the words is alert to are told to change, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker is urged to be watchful about changing his views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges all nine letters of IS ALERT TO; 'to' belongs to the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander was a classical thinker from Stagira.

clue.text: East End murderer, a real tearaway?

explanation.surface: A notorious Victorian killer described as a thorough tearaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper killed in Whitechapel in London's East End; also, a thing that rips is literally a tearer.

clue.text: Firm stayed in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so the word stayed is rearranged

explanation.surface: A company that held on through a difficult patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is stable and unshaking, a synonym.

clue.text: Command to accept in the priesthood

explanation.surface: An instruction about admitting someone to holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree is to order something officially; a bishop also confers holy orders on a new priest with the same verb.

clue.text: Show contempt, but don't giggle at judge

explanation.surface: Advice to show disdain without actually tittering at the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: laugh, but outside the courtroom, not in front of the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something with ridicule as unworthy of serious hearing is an idiom; read literally it means giggling away from the courtroom.

clue.text: Roundheads were their ace rivals fighting

definitions.text: Roundheads were their ace rivals fighting

indicators.note: the words ace rivals are set fighting, so their letters scramble into a new order

explanation.surface: In the Civil War the Parliamentarians were their top opponents in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges ACE RIVALS; the whole clue also describes the answer, the Royalists whom the Roundheads fought in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalist supporters of Charles I in the English Civil War were opposed by Parliament's Roundheads.

clue.text: An extended team is right up close

parts.note: something extended is long
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A team stretched out is pressing right up close to the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beside something means being immediately next to it.

clue.text: Tradesman to Victoria, perhaps, the queen?

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway terminus, an example of a station
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A supplier to Queen Victoria who held a royal warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like the queen but is London's Victoria station; ER is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling paper, pens and writing supplies is one kind of retailer.

clue.text: Pill fit for abstainer to swallow

indicators.note: one piece is told to swallow the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: TT, teetotal, marks someone who abstains from alcohol
fit means able

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is well enough to take medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a compressed dose of medicine, a synonym.

clue.text: Lay out money inside, to our glory

indicators.note: the money letter goes inside the word for laying out

parts.note: to lay out money is to spend it
L stands for pound, the unit of money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spending money on decorations to make our home glorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence or grandeur is the sense shared with glory.

clue.text: Partition, we hear, eccentric person made out of this wood?

indicators.note: signals that the word for partition is only heard, its sound standing in for the spelling

parts.note: a partition is a dividing wall
a nut is a crazy or eccentric person

explanation.surface: A dividing screen, apparently, and an oddball both carved from this timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard brown timber of the tree Juglans is prized for furniture.

clue.text: Something flashy on the road?

parts.note: suggests a showy car or driver, but means the lamp on a vehicle's front that flashes

explanation.surface: A showy car cruising down the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Front lamps on a car are flashed at other drivers on the road.

clue.text: Humiliating failure, if backing a second firm

indicators.note: backing puts the word if into reverse

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm suffers embarrassment if it backs a minor partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete, ludicrous failure or debacle is the meaning.

clue.text: One alone gets strange amount in change

parts.note: strange means odd

indicators.note: the word amount is in change, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A loner receives a peculiar sum in his change.
explanation.definitionFit: The person excluded from a group, the one who does not fit, is left alone.

clue.text: Moving air, plus it is a religious song

indicators.note: moving letters about rearranges them, here air, plus and it

explanation.surface: A stirring tune and, what is more, it is sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' and 'air' both look musical, but 'Moving' rearranges AIR, PLUS and IT; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional African-American sacred folk song is a gospel hymn of this kind.

clue.text: Prize beauty, and avoid mundane affairs?

parts.note: to miss is to avoid
worldly matters, as opposed to spiritual ones, are the world

explanation.surface: An award-winning beauty who shuns everyday concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: The international pageant crowns a winning beauty queen each year.

clue.text: Shoot American friend

explanation.surface: An order to fire at a US pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A young plant growth sprouting is a new shoot; in US slang a pal or buddy is addressed with this.

clue.text: Forbid graduate to take note

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
N, for note, is a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Preventing a graduate from taking notes in a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit something is a synonym of to forbid.

clue.text: Society beauty digging up part of garden

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for part of garden is dug up, read from the bottom

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden

explanation.surface: A society girl found excavating a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante, a young upper-class woman coming out in society, is shortened this way.

clue.text: Quite a game, finding the second Severn crossing?

explanation.surface: Building another bridge over the River Severn is quite a task.
explanation.walkthrough: The second Severn Crossing is the later motorway bridge across the River Severn between England and Wales, so literally a copy of a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive card game in which the same deals are replayed at each table; literally a repeated span over a river.

clue.text: Name old boy as a distinguished character

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Naming a former pupil as an eminent person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a wealthy or upper-class personage, a toff.

clue.text: SOS! Arm sunk in bog

indicators.note: sunk suggests something ruined and broken up, so the letters of SOS and arm are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distress call as someone's arm sinks into a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh or swamp is a wet boggy area, a synonym.

clue.text: Squirm when summons is given to ambassador

parts.note: a writ is a court summons
HE, His Excellency, is how an ambassador is addressed

explanation.surface: Someone wriggles uncomfortably as a court order is served on a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and contort the body uncomfortably is a synonym of squirm.

clue.text: Illness unlikely to affect Harry Lime?

definitions.text: Illness unlikely to affect Harry Lime?

parts.words: Illness unlikely to affect Harry Lime?
parts.note: Harry Lime is the villain of The Third Man, but his surname points to the citrus fruit, which sailors ate to prevent a vitamin C deficiency disease

explanation.surface: Wondering which disease the shady character from The Third Man might escape.
explanation.definitionFit: This vitamin C deficiency disease was prevented on ships by limes, hence Brits being called limeys.

clue.text: Waffle-just what's needed when the balloon goes up

definitions.text: just what's needed when the balloon goes up

explanation.surface: Empty talk just when a crisis breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when the balloon goes up' is an idiom for trouble starting, but literally a hot-air balloon rises on heated gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Waffle is empty, pretentious talk; heated gas is what lifts a balloon into the sky.

clue.text: When the field is seeded, he stands frighteningly alone

definitions.text: When the field is seeded, he stands frighteningly alone

parts.words: When the field is seeded, he stands frighteningly alone
parts.note: sounds like a lone sporting seed or a figure in a horror story, but describes a straw figure put up in a sown field to scare off birds

explanation.surface: A lonely, menacing figure standing out in a newly sown field.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed figure of straw and old clothes set in fields frightens crows away.

clue.text: The whole country is at one in a 'no 'to the French

indicators.note: the at-one letters sit in the French word

parts.note: non is French for no
taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: The whole country stands united in voting no to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A people or state taken as a whole is the meaning, synonym of country.

clue.text: Such fierce competition in the razor industry?

definitions.text: Such fierce competition in the razor industry?

parts.words: Such fierce competition in the razor industry?
parts.note: the adjective for ruthless competition is also the name of an old open-bladed razor

explanation.surface: Wondering how ruthless rivalry gets among makers of shaving blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless, merciless rivalry is so described, and an open straight razor shares the name.

clue.text: Find sun a blessing, to some extent, if without power

indicators.note: only part of the words sun a blessing is used, the run lying inside them

explanation.surface: Considering sunshine a gift if you are powerless to do otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the capacity or power to do something is a synonym.

clue.text: Trembling, lady reset balance

indicators.note: trembling suggests shaken about, so the letters of lady reset are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous woman recalibrates the scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighing device with a movable counterpoise on a graduated arm is a type of scales.
